title: Squire Boone's Painted Stone
summary: By spring 1780 Squire Boone planted Painted Stone, Shelby County’s first large station, about two miles north of present Shelbyville on Clear Creek.
bodyMarkdown:
Squire Boone Jr. was Daniel Boone's younger brother and a frontiersman in his own right. [Squire Boone](https://grokipedia.com/page/Squire_Boone) was born in Berks County, Pennsylvania, in 1744 and trained as a gunsmith. He is [credited](https://grokipedia.com/page/Squire_Boone) with the first permanent settlement in what became Shelby County.

## To Kentucky

From 1767 to 1771, Squire went on several long hunts into Kentucky with Daniel. In 1775 he helped Daniel cut the Wilderness Road and settle Boonesborough. He was wounded during the 1778 siege of Boonesborough, then moved his family to the Falls of the Ohio in the spring of 1779.

## The painted stone

[Squire Boone's Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squire_Boone%27s_Station) took its other name from a rock by the creek. Boone had painted his name and the date on it during a 1776 visit, when he first scouted and claimed the land.

Accounts differ on when the station began. One account gives late 1779 or spring 1780; another gives 1779–1780. Boone brought 13 families to the site on the Clear Fork of [Brashears Creek](/stories/taylorsville-on-brashears-creek/), about 2 miles north of present-day [Shelbyville](/stories/shelbyville/). It was the first large settlement in what is now Shelby County.

## War comes to the station

Painted Stone sat in land that Native nations still defended, and the Revolution brought British-backed raids. In April 1781 about 20 Native warriors attacked the fort. Boone was shot in the side and through the bones of his right arm, and the arm stayed an inch and a half shorter than the left for the rest of his life.

In September, warned that a large raid was coming, most settlers left for Linn's Station. Boone was too weak to travel, so his family stayed behind with one other family. On September 13 the refugees were ambushed by Native warriors and British forces under Capt. Alexander McKee. This became known as the [Long Run massacre](https://grokipedia.com/page/long_run_massacre).

## How many died

Accounts of Long Run differ widely. One account, from historical markers and at least one published report, says about 60 people died. Another says about 15 settlers were actually killed, plus 17 of [John Floyd](/stories/john-floyd/)'s men who were ambushed the next day while going to bury them.

## Losing the station

Boone came back in late 1783 and found the station burned to the ground. Over the next year he built a grist mill and sawmill on the site. But his land dealings failed, and in 1786 he lost all his property, including the station, to creditors. He later served in the Virginia legislature and sponsored a bill to charter Louisville.

## Kentucky today

Boone eventually moved to Indiana, where he died in 1815 and was buried in what is now Squire Boone Caverns. In Shelby County, the Painted Stone Settlers hold yearly reenactments near the Long Run site. [Bagdad](/stories/bagdad-how-a-shelby-county-rail-stop-took-over-consolation/) and Shelbyville lie nearby.
